Step by step, the project has created community resilience and social impacts, including the following: (1) in terms of waste innovation, the project has dealt with 1,500 metric tons of caltrop shell waste, producing 38 metric tons of Biochar and cutting down on 140 metric tons of carbon footprint; (2) in terms of charity and promotion, three charity organizations are matched, donating 4,920 Biochar pouches to rehabilitation buses in Tainan City, Pingtung County, and Chiayi County, which benefited 2.543 million rides; (3) in terms of activities and events, 173 environmental tours were arranged, with 4,729 people participating in these events; 61 consensus meetings were held, with 448 people attending; (4)as far as regional revitalization base is concerned, two venues with six functions were set up; (5)as for the caltrop shell industry, 80 aesthetic products in three categories have been created, which can be purchased via nine online shops and ten brick-and-mortar channels.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a cable-driven wrist exoskeleton with enhanced adaptability
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: Robot-assisted rehabilitation has gained popularity in the last two decades. The focus has shifted from end-effector devices to wearable exoskeletons, emphasizing the transition from bulky machines to portable devices. However, technology gap still exists on how to design exoskeletons with high adaptability. This includes ensuring a sufficient degree of freedom and addressing potential offsets between different users. This paper introduces a cable-driven wrist exoskeleton having two degrees of freedom (DoFs) designed to finely adjust for different users by improving the adjustability of the mechanism, reducing misalignment between the robot's rotational center and human wrist joints to achieve high compatibility. In addition, we have eliminated the handlebar design found in existing exoskeletons, opting for a fully wearable design that also tackles common issues such as insufficient degrees of freedom and limited range of movement. Lastly, we incorporate an additional five redundant degrees of freedom (RDoFs) to enable adaptability and self-alignment, addressing the offset between the flexion-extension axis and ulnar-radial deviation, aspects frequently neglected in previous research.

articleTitle: Multi-objective design optimization of permanent magnet motor using NSGA-II
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-objective optimization design for a 3kW permanent magnet motor was proposed, utilizing the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (NSGA-II). The primary objectives were to minimize cogging torque and weight of the motor. Optimization parameters included the air gap, tooth width, york, slot depth, slot width, slot opening, magnet thickness, and magnet width. The NSGA-II algorithm was employed to search for the optimal motor geometries. The cogging torque and weight of the motor were verified using finite element analysis software. After multiple iterative searches, a Pareto-optimal solution set was obtained, enabling users to select an appropriate motor design based on their specific requirements.

articleTitle: AIoT-based smart aerator system for aquaculture
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: Maintaining optimal dissolved oxygen (DO) levels is critical for aquaculture health and productivity. Traditional mechanical aerators, while effective, are energy-intensive, posing significant operational costs. This study introduces an AIoT-based smart aerator system, integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) tech nologies to enhance energy efficiency and sustainability. Utilizing renewable energy sources, the system offers a dual power supply ensuring continuous operation and environmental benefits. This paper outlines the system's design, implementation, and the r esultant reductions in energy consumption and operational costs.

articleTitle: Exploring the digital art exhibition experience with immersive music therapy creation as a performance form
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to understand audience experiences of immersive art performances and their acceptance of music therapy creations. An evaluation scale for immersive music therapy creation exhibition experiences was developed, constructing four dimensions: "viewing motivation," "emotional experience," and "post-viewing evaluation," based on literature and expert recommendations. The research process involved 110 audience members completing paper questionnaires after participating in live events. Correlation analysis was then used to understand the exhibition experience and satisfaction levels across different background variables. The results show that audiences with different personal backgrounds have varying pre-exhibition expectations, which in turn influence their viewing motivations and expectations for immersive performances, as well as their post-viewing satisfaction levels. This study, through the construction of an "Immersive Performance Exhibition Experience Scale," provides a method to evaluate audience viewing motivations and emotional responses. This helps to understand whether immersive music therapy creation performances meet audience needs and identify factors affecting experience satisfaction. It also provides opportunities for discussion and in-depth research in future related studies.

articleTitle: Recognizing spectrogram of machine sounds using convolutional neural networks
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: This study focuses on the application of artificial intelligence to diagnose the operational status of electric machinery by analyzing sound signals. Using a commercial monaural voice recorder, sound signals from an electric air pump were collected in a semi-anechoic chamber at a sampling rate of 44100/sec. The recorded signals were then normalized and processed using wavelet transform to generate spectrograms. Four different signal durations (0.2s, 0.5s, 1s, and 2s) were tested, resulting in 600 spectrograms for each duration. A pre-trained GoogLeNet model, implemented using Matlab's deep learning toolbox, was trained on these spectrograms. The results indicate that the model achieved a recognition accuracy of 93.9% using 1-second spectrograms, with individual fault detection accuracies above 90%, except for NG1 at 86.7%. This approach demonstrates the potential for applying AI-driven sound analysis to fault diagnosis in various types of electric machinery.

articleTitle: Image denoising using min-max filtering and self-attention neural networks
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: Digital images may be subjected to electromagnetic interference during transmission and camera component damage, resulting in image quality degradation due to pulse noise interference. How to effectively restore the images interfered with by salt-and-pepper (SAP) noise is essential to improve the quality of digital images. This paper proposes using minimum-maximum filtering and self-attention neural networks (SANN) to remove the SAP noise in the deteriorated images. Firstly, the noise density of the image is estimated. If it is a slight or mildly noisy image, the noise pixels are reconstructed using a SANN. Conversely, if it is a medium or high noise-density interference, max-pooling and min-pooling, through several iterations, generate min-max pooling. Finally, min-max pooled images are composed by mean filtering. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively reconstruct the image interfered with by various noise densities and outperform many state-of-the-art algorithms by visualization and objective measurement tests.

articleTitle: The impact of new communication technologies on digital video production - take Kun-Shan University public relations and advertising department for example
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: Communication technology refers to humans using tools, materials, products, and systems to enhance their communication capabilities. Benefiting from increasingly powerful software, it accelerates the speed of information transmission and transforms our environment into an information society. With the development of artificial intelligence, the boundaries and targets of communication have expanded from merely human-to-human interaction to human-machine communication. Mediation tools between humans and machines have evolved into objects of communication themselves, allowing for more effective communication through machines or software. This, in turn, impacts digital video production and content. This study specifically focuses on the industry-Academia collaboration project of the Department of Public Relations and Advertising at Kun-Shan University, investigating client satisfaction with video content and how students apply new communication technologies in video production.

articleTitle: Microstructure of FeMnAINiCr shape memory alloys
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: This study is to investigate the microstructure of the FeMnAINiCr alloy under different heat treatment conditions. The microstructure shows that few cracks are appeared after the sample was heat treated at 1100°C for 1 hour. Many cracks are generated in the sample after heated treatment at 1200°C for 1 hour.

articleTitle: A study of multi-task learning using a VoVNet-OSA block enhanced U-Net on the Med++ MNIST dataset
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: In this study, we propose a multi-task learning framework using a modified VoVNet-OSA Block Enhanced UNet, named VovUnet_Var, for image segmentation and classification on the Med++ MNIST dataset. VovUnet_Var features downsampling (DownOsa) and upsampling (UpOsa) blocks, with a classification head. The architecture sequentially downscales the input image to capture hierarchical features and uses adaptive average pooling and a fully connected layer for classification. For segmentation, upsampling layers restore spatial dimensions, producing segmentation masks. This model effectively handles complex medical imaging tasks, providing a robust solution for simultaneous image segmentation and classification.

articleTitle: Applying deep learning for sentiment analysis: a case study of prediction 2023 president election
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: This study scenario is to explore the 2023 presidential election via applying deep learning for social sentiment analysis. We compare several deep learning models, including CNN, RNN, and BERT, focusing on word presentation to improve performance. The results show that BERT outperforms other model combinations overall, and CNN is influential for positive sentiment. The study offers insights for future research and aims to impact social sentiment and public relations positively.

articleTitle: Implementation of campus unmanned guided vehicle using YOLO network with LiDAR positioning
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: Existing campus tour systems mainly rely on landmarks, static maps, and manual tours, which cannot be updated in real-time and are limited by human resources, resulting in an inefficient tour guide system and a poor visitor experience. This researc h aims to realize a driverless campus tour vehicle that can interact with visitors and show them the way. This paper utilizes the Raspberry Pi and the Pi Racer to achieve autonomous navigation, obstacle avoidance, and automatic speed control. Using YOLO net to recognize the campus buildings and speech recognition to interact with the unmanned guided vehicle enhances campus friendliness.

articleTitle: Study on the interference effects of offshore wind farm arrays on GCA radar at specific detection heights
publicationTitle: IET International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Applications (ICETA 2024)
abstract: This study has investigated the impact of a 4x4 offshore wind turbine array setup on the operation of S-band Ground-Controlled Approach (GCA) radar in a specific region. The research presents the radar detection status corresponding to stratified altitudes ranging from 500 feet to 4,000 feet. The study identifies the formation of interference zones within certain areas and employs numerical simulations to pre-determine the locations of clear airspace zones. Future work can integrate professional insights from air traffic controllers to develop and apply numerical learning techniques.
